bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar Introduces Performance Assessment Index for Banks - Drishti IAS
bihar_raw_news.content: Bihar Prev Next Bihar Introduces Performance Assessment Index for Banks 27 Oct 2026 2 min read Why in News? The Bihar government has introduced a 100-point performance assessment index to evaluate banks operating in the state. IDFC FIRST Bank topped the ranking with 74 points. Key Points Performance Assessment Index: Banks have been classified into three zones based on their scores: Green Zone: Includes 11 banks scoring 50 or above. Yellow Zone: Comprises 7 banks. Red Zone: Contains several banks, including public sector banks. Annual Credit Plan 2026–27: Bihar has set a credit disbursement target of ₹4.95 lakh crore . By 30 th September 2026, banks had disbursed ₹1.89 lakh crore, achieving 38.25% of the target. Credit disbursement to Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) reached ₹84,091 crore, while agricultural credit disbursement stood at ₹43,967 crore. Credit-Deposit Ratio (CDR): Bihar's CDR stood at 60.17% as of 30 th September 2026 . The state government urged banks to increase lending within the state, clear pending loan applications and improve credit access, particularly under the Kisan Credit Card and PM Vishwakarma schemes. Credit-Deposit Ratio The Credit-Deposit Ratio (CDR) is the ratio of a bank's total loans and advances to its total deposits, expressed as a percentage. It indicates the extent to which deposits mobilised by banks are converted into credit. bihar_raw_news.title: ICAR-MGIFRI, Motihari Promotes Sustainable Orchard Management under Khet Bachao ...
bihar_raw_news.content: 27 October 2026, East Champaran, Bihar ICAR–Mahatma Gandhi Integrated Farming Research Institute, Motihari, Bihar, organised a farmer awareness and field interaction programme under Khet Bachao Abhiyan 2026 at Kothia Hariram village, Mehsi Block, East Champaran, today. The programme focused on promoting judicious fertilizer use, soil health management, nutrient recycling, crop diversification and sustainable management of mango and litchi orchards. The programme under Khet Bachao Abhiyan 2026 emphasized soil-test-based nutrient management, balanced fertilization and sustainable orchard management to enhance mango and litchi productivity while maintaining long-term soil fertility. Farmers were sensitized to the importance of recycling organic resources such as crop residues, fallen leaves, farmyard manure and compost, along with the judicious use of mineral fertilizers. The programme also highlighted intercropping and crop diversification as strategies to improve land-use efficiency, generate supplementary income and strengthen farmers’ livelihoods. Emphasis was placed on efficient resource utilization, reduced input costs, improved soil health and enhanced resilience to climatic and economic uncertainties. Interactive discussions addressed farmers’ challenges and promoted practical, economically viable and environmentally sustainable orchard management practices. Through this initiative, ICAR-MGIFRI reaffirmed its commitment to promoting sustainable horticulture, soil health and farmers’ self-reliance in the mango- and litchi-growing regions of East Champaran, Bihar. A total of 29 farmers and participants attended the programme and interacted on improved orchard management and efficient utilization of locally available resources. (Source: Press Information Bureau, New Delhi)

According to the ministry, the settlements were facilitated through constructive dialogue and the active participation and cooperation of the employees’ organisations and the bank management, helping resolve the disputes amicably and strengthen industrial harmony. bihar_raw_news.content: Bihar Museum in Patna has been placed ninth on a list of the world’s 100 best museums, ahead of every other Asian museum. It is placed at number 1 in Asia. The 2026 ranking comes from the travel guide Worth a Journey and covers museums of art, history, science, technology and open-air heritage across the globe. Mexico City’s Museo Nacional de Antropología leads the list, followed by Madrid’s Museo del Prado and Denmark’s Louisiana Museum of Modern Art. The State Hermitage in Saint Petersburg, Vienna’s Kunsthistorisches Museum and the Şanlıurfa Archaeology Museum in Turkey take the next three places. Two Second World War museums, one in Gdańsk and one in New Orleans, sit just above Patna, while New York’s Metropolitan Museum of Art follows at 10th. Bihar Museum is the only Indian museum in the entire 100. A model depicting Sher Shah Suri’s regime at the Children’s Gallery of Bihar Museum, Patna. (Photo: www.biharmuseum.org) The guide describes it as a modern state museum that follows the story of Bihar from the Stone Age to the present day. Visitors move through chronological galleries filled with sculptures, coins, manuscripts and folk art. The building itself is spacious, with open courtyards and lawns that give the collection room to breathe. A short film on the region’s history helps set the scene before the galleries begin. bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar to seek Centre's aid to clear flood-hit farmlands, fisheries of sand and silt
bihar_raw_news.content: Governance 1 min Read Bihar to seek Centre's aid to clear flood-hit farmlands, fisheries of sand and silt The state Disaster Management Department (DMD) has asked district magistrates (DMs) of 22 districts to assess sand and silt deposits on flood-affected agricultural land and fisheries caused by the floods in Ganga, Son, Gandak, Kosi and other rivers. PTI Published On Oct 27, 2026 at 08:55 PM IST Select ETGovernment as Preferred Choice on Google Share Icon Copy Link Share on Whatsapp Share on Linkedin Share on X Share on Telegram Share on Facebook Bookmark Comment The worst-affected districts included Patna, Bhojpur, Saran, Vaishali, Bhagalpur, Begusarai, Buxar, Samastipur, Munger, Katihar, Lakhisarai, Khagaria, Purnia, Madhepura and Araria. The Bihar government will seek funds from the Centre to remove sand and silt from farmlands and fisheries affected in the recent floods in the state, an official statement said on Tuesday. The state Disaster Management Department (DMD) has asked district magistrates (DMs) of 22 districts to assess sand and silt deposits on flood-affected agricultural land and fisheries caused by the floods in Ganga, Son, Gandak, Kosi and other rivers. "Acting on the chief minister's directions, the DMD has written to the DMs of Patna, Bhojpur, Saran, Vaishali, Bhagalpur, Begusarai, Buxar, Samastipur, Munger, Katihar, Lakhisarai, Khagaria, Purnia, Madhepura, Arwal, West and East Champaran, Gopalganj, Darbhanga, Muzaffarpur, Supaul and Saharsa, directing them to assess sand and silt deposits on agricultural land and in fisheries affected by recent floods," the statement said. The department asked authorities concerned to conduct on-site inspection of the affected agricultural land and fisheries and assess the extent of sand and silt deposition. "Based on this assessment, financial assistance will be sought in accordance with prescribed relief norms of the State Disaster Response Fund (SDRF) and the National Disaster Response Fund (NDRF)," it said. This assistance will help restore and facilitate agricultural and fisheries-related activities in the affected areas, it added. Around 50 lakh people across several Bihar districts were affected by the recent floods, which also damaged agricultural land and fisheries, officials said. The worst-affected districts included Patna, Bhojpur, Saran, Vaishali, Bhagalpur, Begusarai, Buxar, Samastipur, Munger, Katihar, Lakhisarai, Khagaria, Purnia, Madhepura and Araria. bihar_raw_news.title: PM Modi likely to inaugurate Bhuj–Barauni Amrit Bharat Express during Gujarat trip - Mint
bihar_raw_news.content: PM Modi likely to inaugurate Bhuj–Barauni Amrit Bharat Express during Gujarat trip: Check frequency, route, major stops An Amrit Bharat Express linking Bhuj, Gujarat, and Barauni, Bihar, is expected to begin running ahead of Diwali. PM Modi may flag it off during his Gujarat visit, though his official itinerary does not list the inauguration. Livemint Published 27 Oct 2026, 07:30 PM IST Prefer Livemint on Google AI-generated image. For representational purposes only. AI Quick Read Prime Minister Narendra Modi is likely to flag off an Amrit Bharat Express train on October 30 when he visits Gujarat, as per a report by Gujarat Samachar. This train, numbered 19427/19428, will start operations ahead of Diwali, and will run between Gujarat's Bhuj and Bihar's Barauni. Its total route will be 2,532-km long and will connect four states, namely, Gujarat, Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh, and Bihar. However, the PM's official itinerary does not mention this train inauguration. Modi will be on a two-day Gujarat visit from October 30 during which he will inaugurate and launch development projects of Banas Dairy and attend the National Unity Day parade at the Statue of Unity, the state government said on Tuesday, as per news agency PTI. Service to operate thrice a week The 19427 Bhuj-Barauni Amrit Bharat Express will depart from Bhuj at 5:30 pm and will take 58 hours and 35 minutes to reach Barauni. While returning, the 19428 Barauni-Bhuj Amrit Bharat Express will depart at 11:55 at tnight and reach Bhij at 1:15 pm on the fourth day after journey of 61 hours and 20 minutes. The Bhuj-Barauni service will operate on Monday, Wednesday and Saturday, while the Barauni-Bhuj service will operate on Tuesday, Thursday and Saturday. Which are some of the major stations this service will connect? The new service will have commercial stoppages at several important stations en route, including Samakhiali, Ahmedabad, Ratlam, Kota, Sawai Madhopur, Gangapur City, Bharatpur, Mathura, Hathras, Bareilly, Izzatnagar, Pilibhit, Lakhimpur, Gonda, Gorakhpur, Siwan, Chhapra, Hajipur, Muzaffarpur and Samastipur, among others. The new train service will provide an additional rail travel option between western and eastern parts of the country and improve connectivity for passengers travelling between Gujarat, Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh and Bihar. With the train launching ahead of Diwali , it is expected to benefit a large number of workers from UP and Bihar who are employed in Gujarat's industrial centres like Kutch, Ahmedabad, Morbi, and Vadodara. Amrit Bharat Express: What does it offer? The Amrit Bharat Express is a modern non-AC long-distance sleeper class train for affordable travel within India. These trains come with 11 General Class coaches, 8 Sleeper Class coaches, 1 Pantry Car, and 2 Second Class–cum–Luggage–cum–Guard Vans with disabled-friendly compartments. Fares are generally ₹ 500 for every 1,000 km, and there is no dynamic pricing, thus ensuring accessibility for the common passenger. As per the railways, this enhanced connectivity supports employment mobility, tourism, trade, and access to education and healthcare. bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar e-Challans Now Block RC Renewal, Fitness Certificates and Transfers - Urban Acres
bihar_raw_news.content: Home Breaking News Bihar e-Challans Now Block RC Renewal, Fitness Certificates and Transfers Breaking News Bihar e-Challans Now Block RC Renewal, Fitness Certificates and Transfers By Harpreet Singh October 27, 2026 0 Copy URL Facebook Linkedin X WhatsApp Bihar will restrict key transport services for vehicles with unpaid e-challans, including registration certificate renewal, fitness certification and ownership transfers, under enforcement instructions issued by the state transport department on October 27. State transport commissioner Arif Ahsan directed district transport officers and other concerned authorities to act against vehicles with pending traffic fines in accordance with the Supreme Court’s directions. Vehicles with unpaid dues may also be blacklisted on the transport department’s online portal until the fines are cleared. The restrictions will cover renewal of registration certificates, issuance of duplicate RCs and updates to a vehicle owner’s correspondence address. The department will also stop ownership transfers for vehicles with outstanding e-challans, preventing owners from selling or formally transferring such vehicles until the dues are settled. “Under the new enforcement measures, online transport services linked to vehicles with unpaid e-challans will be restricted,” Ahsan said. He added that issuance of fitness certificates and other related documents would also be affected. The department has further ordered restrictions on pollution certificates and updated repair or fitness-related certificates where vehicles have pending fines. The measures will apply to vehicles identified through the transport portal and will be supported by regular and random checks by enforcement officials. The action is also intended to target repeat traffic offenders. Officials have been instructed to act against driving licence holders who repeatedly violate traffic rules, including suspension of licences and restrictions on renewal wherever applicable. If a vehicle is found during a check to have an unpaid or non-complied e-challan, officials may seize it under applicable provisions. Transport Secretary Raj Kumar said effective enforcement of traffic rules was essential to improving road safety. He said action against vehicles with pending e-challans would be taken in accordance with the Supreme Court’s directions, adding that the objective was not only to recover fines but also to promote responsibility and discipline among motorists, reduce traffic violations and help prevent road accidents. The instructions place online transport services at the centre of Bihar’s traffic-fine enforcement system. A pending challan can now affect several routine vehicle transactions, including documentation, certification and ownership changes, rather than remaining only an unpaid penalty. Ahsan directed officials to conduct regular and random checks, identify vehicles with pending challans and take action under the prescribed provisions. The department’s instructions did not specify a separate deadline for vehicle owners to clear existing dues before the restrictions take effect. bihar_raw_news.content: How India’s Siang Dam Worth Rs 1 Lakh Crore Can Counter China's Rs 14 Lakh Crore Brahmaputra Project? Why is Arunachal Opposing? By Jaisal Kaur Last Updated: Oct 27, 2026, 18:21 IST China started construction of its Yarlung Tsangpo hydropower project in July 2025. The project is slated to comprise five cascade hydropower stations, with an investment of 1.2 trillion yuan, or approximately $167.8 billion. Its envisioned capability is around 60,000 MW, making it one of the world's largest hydropower projects. Yarlung Tsangpo River in Tibet India's proposed Siang Upper Multipurpose Project (SUMP) in Arunachal Pradesh has acquired strategic relavence amid China's construction of a massive hydropower project on the Yarlung Tsangpo River in Tibet. The Indian project, with a potential capability of 11,200 megawatts (MW), is being regarded as a possible safeguard for water security, flood management and electricity generation. However, concerns over displacement, environmental damage and the loss of ancestral land have ignited protests among local communities. Why China's Mega Dam Raises Concerns China started construction of its Yarlung Tsangpo hydropower project in July 2025. The project is slated to comprise five cascade hydropower stations, with an investment of 1.2 trillion yuan, or approximately $167.8 billion. Its envisioned capability is around 60,000 MW, making it one of the world's largest hydropower projects. The Yarlung Tsangpo flows from Tibet into Arunachal Pradesh, where it is called as the Siang, before joining other rivers to form the Brahmaputra in Assam. Since China's project is situated upstream, Indian authorities are intrigued about the possible impact of reservoir operations on downstream water flows. Although a dam cannot simply stop the Brahmaputra's flow, its operation could impact the timing and volume of water releases. This has ignited concerns about seasonal water availability, instant discharges and flood management. How India's Siang Project Could Help The proposed SUMP with estimated cost of around Rs 1.13 lakh crore is developed as a storage-based multipurpose project consisting of hydropower generation with water storage and flow regulation. According to figures cited by Arunachal Pradesh Deputy Chief Minister Chowna Mein, the project could offer approximately 9.2 billion cubic metres of live storage. The proposed reservoir could possibly regulate river flows and handle extreme water releases, depending on its design and operating settlements. The project could also bolster India's electricity supply and promote infrastructure development in the Northeast. However, its construction has not been cleared, and its feasibility remains under review. Why Local Communities in Arunachal Pradesh Oppose the Project The proposed dam is seeing resistance from indigenous Adi communities and other natives of the Siang Valley. Protesters fear the disruption of ancestral land, displacement, ecological damage, livelihoods and cultural property. Protests turned into violence in October 2026, thus triggering additional security deployment in the region. The controversy has underscored the hurdle of balancing national security needs with the rights and grievances of local communities. What Lies Ahead? bihar_raw_news.content: Home Breaking News Gaya-Bangkok Flight Launch Opens New Route for Bihar Tourism Breaking News Gaya-Bangkok Flight Launch Opens New Route for Bihar Tourism By Maria Dsouza October 27, 2026 0 Copy URL Facebook Linkedin X WhatsApp Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary on Monday flagged off IndiGo’s first non-stop flight from Gaya to Bangkok, adding a twice-weekly international service aimed at improving access to Bodh Gaya and strengthening air links between Bihar and Thailand. The flight was inaugurated through videoconferencing at a ceremony in Patna. Choudhary greeted passengers on the inaugural service and said the new connection would strengthen religious, cultural and tourism ties between Bihar and Thailand. Gaya is the principal air gateway to Bodh Gaya, one of the world’s most important Buddhist pilgrimage destinations. The chief minister said the direct service would make travel easier for international visitors and support tourism across the Magadh region. The route is being launched ahead of the pilgrim season, when Gaya Airport is preparing for an increase in domestic and foreign tourist movement under its winter schedule. The new service is expected to support hotels, transport operators, handicraft businesses and other enterprises dependent on tourism. Choudhary said improved air connectivity would help Bihar give wider international recognition to its cultural heritage, historical sites and local products. The launch is part of a broader state effort to expand aviation access through airports in Patna, Darbhanga, Gaya and Purnia. Choudhary said the state was working on a policy to increase connectivity on new international routes, with expected support from IndiGo. He also said coordination to expand international air services in Bihar would continue. Gaya’s international network has expanded in recent days. Thailand-based Thai Airways began direct flights to Bangkok over the weekend, while Thai AirAsia started a service connecting Gaya with Don Mueang. Thai AirAsia’s flights are scheduled to operate three days a week—Tuesday, Friday and Sunday—until March 26, 2027. Domestic connectivity has also increased. Air India began two services on the Delhi-Gaya-Delhi route from Sunday, with the airline’s winter schedule scheduled to remain in operation until March 27, 2027. The expansion gives pilgrims and tourists more direct travel options during the period of higher seasonal demand. It also places additional importance on the ability of Gaya Airport and local tourism-linked services to manage international arrivals, onward transport and visitor requirements. The state government’s proposed international connectivity policy is expected to guide further route expansion. national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi today held a bilateral meeting with the Acting Head of State of the Principality of Liechtenstein, Hereditary Prince Alois, at Hyderabad House in New Delhi. Both the leaders discussed cooperation in various areas, including trade and investment, science, technology and innovation and people-to-people exchanges. They also exchanged views on regional and global developments. Prince Alois was accorded a ceremonial reception at the forecourt of Rashtrapati Bhavan this morning. President Droupadi Murmu and Prime Minister Narendra Modi welcomed him. In a media statement, Prince Alois said that the visit bears testimony to the importance that Liechtenstein attaches to the relationship with India. He said that the conclusion of the trade and economic partnership agreement, TEPA, with India, which entered into force a year ago, marked a significant milestone in this regard. He further said that Liechtenstein is determined to build on this momentum and strengthen ties with India even further. Prince Alois also expressed gratitude to Prime Minister Narendra Modi for the invitation. Prince Alois and his spouse, Princess Sophie, also paid homage to Mahatma Gandhi at Raj Ghat in New Delhi. He will also meet President Droupadi Murmu at Rashtrapati Bhavan this evening, who will also host an official banquet in the honour of the visiting dignitary. The acting Head of State of the Principality of Liechtenstein arrived in New Delhi yesterday from Vadodara. Union Minister Jayant Singh received him at the airport. He was accompanied by his spouse, Princess Sophie and a high-level official, as well as a business delegation comprising top industry leaders. This is the second visit of Prince Alois to India in 2026. He earlier visited New Delhi in February this year to attend the AI Impact Summit. He had previously visited India in 2010 and 2018. Ministry of External Affairs said the visit is expected to provide further impetus to the growing engagement between India and Liechtenstein, particularly since operationalization of the India-EFTA Trade and Economic Partnership Agreement last year. The visit will provide an opportunity to further deepen the friendly ties between India and Liechtenstein and build partnerships in new areas of mutual interest.

national_raw_news.title: Polling underway in Israel to elect new Parliament
national_raw_news.content: Polling is underway across Israel, with voters choosing representatives to the country’s 120-member Knesset. With 7.3 million eligible voters and 36 parties contesting the election, the outcome will determine the balance of power in parliament. Voting will end at 10 pm local time tonight. The election comes amid intense debate over national security, the October 7, 2023, Hamas attacks, military service and the country’s future political direction. The election is widely viewed as a test of Netanyahu’s leadership, with opposition figures, including former military chief Gadi Eisenkot and former prime minister Naftali Bennett, seeking to challenge his right-wing coalition. Israel follows a nationwide proportional representation system in which the entire country constitutes a single electoral constituency. Political parties must secure at least 3.25% of the national vote to enter the Knesset. Netanyahu, leader of the right-wing Likud party, has served as prime minister for nearly 19 years across three separate periods since 1996. Former Israel Defence Forces chief of staff Gadi Eisenkot, who leads the centrist Yashar party, has emerged as one of Netanyahu’s principal challengers. Former prime minister Naftali Bennett is leading the B’Yachad electoral alliance, which includes former prime minister Yair Lapid’s Yesh Atid party. Other significant political players include Yair Golan’s left-leaning Democrats, Avigdor Liberman’s Yisrael Beiteinu and Arab-led parties such as Ra’am and the Joint List.

national_raw_news.title: 12th BRICS Parliamentary Forum concludes with unanimous Joint Declaration
national_raw_news.content: The 12th BRICS Parliamentary Forum concluded today with the adoption of the Joint Declaration unanimously. The Joint Declaration reflects the BRICS member nations’ commitment to further strengthening parliamentary cooperation and advancing their shared objectives under the four key themes – Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability. During the second and final day of the two-day Forum, Lok Sabha Speaker and Chairperson of the 12th BRICS Parliamentary Forum Om Birla proposed the unanimous adoption of the Joint Declaration. After that, Mr Birla handed over the Chairship of the BRICS Forum for 2027 to China. Later, Mr Birla delivered his valedictory address at Central Hall of Samvidhan Sadan, in which he called for greater dialogue, trust and cooperation among nations to address global challenges. Mr. Birla said that despite differences in opinions, backgrounds and challenges, BRICS countries share a common commitment to human welfare, peace and prosperity. Mr. Birla emphasised the need to respect the sovereignty of every nation, resolve international disputes peacefully and ensure equitable development opportunities for all. The Lok Sabha Speaker said that during the two-day forum, the discussions focused not only on current challenges but also on exploring new avenues for future cooperation. Highlighting the prevailing global conflicts, regional instability and economic uncertainty, Mr. Birla stressed that dialogue and cooperation are more important than ever. He said India believes that lasting solutions to global problems can be achieved through dialogue rather than conflict, peace rather than war, and cooperation rather than competition. He added that global peace must guarantee security, dignity and justice, along with the promise of a better future for everyone, particularly the younger generation. Mr Birla said that through the joint declaration, the participating countries reaffirmed their commitment to the principles of the United Nations Charter, sovereign equality of nations, mutual respect, non-interference in internal affairs and the peaceful settlement of international disputes. He said, the declaration also strongly condemned all acts of terrorism and called for coordinated and concrete action against all terrorists and terrorist organisations. Emphasising the use of Artificial Intelligence, Mr. Birla said its application should be guided by the principles of ethics, transparency, accountability and human welfare. He stressed that technology should improve human life and its development must remain aligned with human values. Mr. Birla said the success of BRICS should not be limited to the progress of its member countries but should also have a positive impact on the wider global community. He emphasised that the aspirations of the Global South must receive due consideration in global decision-making processes. The 12th BRICS Parliamentary Forum began yesterday with the theme Fostering Parliaments for People-Centric Development.

national_raw_news.title: PM Modi to hold bilateral meeting with Liechtenstein Prince Alois
national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi and the Acting Head of State of the Principality of Liechtenstein, Hereditary Prince Alois, will hold a bilateral meeting in New Delhi today. The acting Head of State of the Principality of Liechtenstein, who is on a three-day visit to India, arrived in New Delhi yesterday from Vadodara. He is accompanied by his spouse, Princess Sophie, and a high-level official, as well as a business delegation comprising top industry leaders. Prime Minister Narendra Modi and the Acting Head of State of the Principality of Liechtenstein will discuss cooperation in various areas including trade and investment, science, technology and innovation and people-to-people exchanges. They will also exchange views on regional and global developments. Prince Alois will be accorded a ceremonial reception at the forecourt of Rashtrapati Bhavan this morning. He will also meet President Droupadi Murmu at Rashtrapati Bhavan this evening, who will also host an official banquet in the honour of the visiting dignitary. External Affairs Minister Dr. S Jaishankar will also call on Prince Alois. This is the second visit of Prince Alois to India in 2026. He earlier visited New Delhi in February this year to attend the AI Impact Summit. The Ministry of External Affairs said that the visit is expected to provide further impetus to the growing engagement between India and Liechtenstein, particularly since operationalization of the India-EFTA Trade and Economic Partnership Agreement last year. The visit will provide an opportunity to further deepen the friendly ties between India and Liechtenstein and build partnerships in new areas of mutual interest.

national_raw_news.title: 12th BRICS Parliamentary Forum to conclude today in New Delhi
national_raw_news.content: The two-day 12th BRICS Parliamentary Forum will conclude in New Delhi today. Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla, who is also the Chairperson of the Forum, will deliver the valedictory speech after the adoption of the joint statement. Thereafter, the presidency will be handed over to China. Vice President C P Radhakrishnan will host lunch in honour of the presiding officers and leaders of the delegation of Member and Partner Countries. The second and final day of the forum will begin with the fourth plenary on Sustainability: The role of parliaments in fostering a sustainable and inclusive future for our nations. The 12th BRICS Parliamentary Forum began yesterday with the theme “Fostering Parliaments for People-Centric Development. Prime Minister Narendra Modi interacted with MPs from BRICS nations during the Forum. They exchanged perspectives on a wide range of issues. In his inaugural address, Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla called upon the Parliaments of BRICS member and partner countries to strengthen their collective resolve towards people-centric development, global peace, sustainability and international cooperation. Emphasizing the transformative potential of parliamentary engagement, he underscored the need to harness the collective wisdom of nations to address shared challenges, deepen mutual understanding and bring meaningful, positive change to the lives of citizens. Mr Birla also addressed the First Plenary Session of the Forum, which focused on the Critical Role of Parliaments in Strengthening Institutional Resilience for a Better Future. Addressing the Second Plenary Session focusing on Harnessing Parliaments for Promoting Human-centric Innovation in Artificial Intelligence and Digital Technologies, Mr Birla said, from Artificial Intelligence to Digital Transformation, the challenge is not merely to embrace emerging technologies but to ensure that they serve humanity, promote inclusive growth, expand equal opportunities and empower citizens. The third plenary was on Cooperation: Leveraging Parliamentary cooperation for a more representative global governance architecture. On the sidelines of the 12th BRICS Parliamentary Forum 2026, Mr Birla today held bilateral meetings with the Speaker of the Federal National Council of the UAE, Mr Saqr Ghobash; Vice Chairman of the National People’s Congress of China, Mr Zheng Jianbang; and a member of the Praesidium of the Islamic Consultative Assembly of Iran, Mr Ahmed Naderi. During the meeting between Om Birla and the Speaker of the Federal National Council of the UAE, Saqr Ghobash, both sides reaffirmed their commitment to further strengthening the historic bonds of friendship between India and the UAE through enhanced parliamentary cooperation, regular dialogue and exchanges of parliamentary delegations. They also exchanged views on regional developments and underscored the importance of dialogue and diplomacy in promoting peace and stability. During the meeting between Om Birla and Vice Chairman of the National People’s Congress of China, Zheng Jianbang, the two leaders discussed strengthening India-China relations through parliamentary exchanges, regular dialogue and cooperation in areas such as education, healthcare and technology. Mr Birla emphasised that, as neighbours, these two countries have a shared responsibility to maintain peace and tranquillity along the border and resolve differences amicably through dialogue and mutual respect. During his meeting with the Member of the Praesidium of the Islamic Consultative Assembly of Iran, Ahmed Naderi, Mr Birla emphasised the importance of peace and stability in the region for the welfare of humanity and highlighted the role of parliamentary dialogue and bilateral engagements in advancing these shared objectives. The two sides also discussed taking forward Chabahar Port cooperation through joint efforts. Mr. Naderi expressed gratitude for the medicines, assistance and other support extended by India to Iran.

national_raw_news.title: EC defends SIR of electoral rolls before Supreme Court
national_raw_news.content: The Election Commission has defended its Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls before the Supreme Court, maintaining that the exercise was authorised by law and the relevant orders were approved unanimously by all three members of the Commission. Rejecting the allegations that Form 6 had been amended, the poll panel, in its 248-page response to the petition against the chief election commissioner (CEC), said that no changes were made to the statutory Form 6 used for voter registration. A bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant is scheduled to hear on Tuesday petitions against CEC Gyanesh Kumar and the decisions taken by the poll panel during the SIR. In a counter-affidavit, the poll body sought summary dismissal of the petitions and called the allegations misconceived, which rested on a single newspaper report. The affidavit, filed by Deputy Election Commissioner Bhanu Prakash Yeturu on behalf of the Commission said attempt to make aspersions against the Election Commission is unfortunate. It said the affidavit itself had been approved for filing by a unanimous decision of all three members of the Commission. The Affidavit said the three SIR orders were issued in accordance with decisions of the EC arrived at unanimously and taken in due compliance with Article 324 of the Constitution of India. The poll body said any suggestion, observation or query raised by a commissioner while a file is being processed does not constitute a decision of the Commission. On the Form 6 row, the EC said it unequivocally rejects the misleading contention that the statutory form had been changed. It added that Form 6 is an application through which an eligible person seeks inclusion in the electoral rolls According to the affidavit, the declaration attached during the SIR is a separate document provided by the SIR orders and “is not a part of Form 6. It said the declaration used in the Bihar SIR was later replaced in the subsequent orders so that applicants could give details of themselves and their parents or grandparents from the 2002-03 rolls and avoid submitting further documents once successfully mapped. The poll body also said that appeals filed in West Bengal against orders including electors in the rolls were filed by officers of the state chief electoral officer’s office acting as statutory authorities in line with the apex court’s orders, and that ” matters were not brought to the Commission. Questioning the maintainability of the pleas, the Commission said, in the eyes of law, a newspaper report is not treated as evidence of the facts it narrates. The Commission added that it has “neither released nor authorised the release of any internal note/ file to any news agency. Citing Article 324(5) of the Constitution, which protects the CEC from removal except in the manner of a Supreme Court judge, the EC said any prayer to restrain the CEC from functioning was not maintainable. It also rejected the petitioner’s contentions on electronic voting machines (EVMs). The EC said similar challenges had been rejected by the top court several times.

national_raw_news.title: PM Modi will inaugurate ESTIC 2026 today at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi
national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi will inaugurate the Emerging Science, Technology and Innovation Conclave ESTIC 2026 today at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi. He will also address the gathering on the occasion. The three-day Conclave will bring together leading scientists, researchers, academicians, policymakers, industry leaders, startups and international experts to deliberate on emerging technologies and India’s science, technology and innovation priorities. The deliberations will span 12 thematic areas, including artificial intelligence, biotechnology, advanced materials, manufacturing, healthcare, energy, climate and ocean sciences. Discussions will focus on research priorities, national capabilities and translating scientific advances into practical applications. The Conclave will also feature an extensive technology and innovation exhibition showcasing indigenous scientific achievements and emerging technologies. It will include around 150 deep-tech startup stalls, which will highlight technological developments and their potential applications across sectors. The Conclave will also use thematic videos, technology demonstrations, documentaries, informational kiosks and augmented and virtual reality experiences to enhance engagement with scientific developments and their real-world applications. A new initiative, the Global Connect Networking Event, will bring together more than 300 invited participants from academia, research institutions and industry in India and abroad. It will provide a platform to explore international research partnerships, industry-academia collaboration and pathways for translating innovations from laboratories to markets.

national_raw_news.title: Cyclone Arnab moving towards Andhra Pradesh coast 51 mins ago 25
national_raw_news.content: Very Severe Cyclonic Storm Arnab over the Bay of Bengal is moving towards the Andhra Pradesh coast, with landfall expected tomorrow morning. Odisha is bracing for heavy to extremely heavy rainfall, particularly in its southern districts, as the storm approaches the eastern coastline. The State Government has intensified preparedness, while several train services have been cancelled or curtailed as a precaution. The weather has changed across southern and coastal Odisha under the influence of Very Severe Cyclonic Storm Arnab. Rain has started in southern Odisha, while coastal districts are witnessing cloudy skies as the cyclone moves closer to the eastern coast. The India Meteorological Department has warned of extremely heavy rainfall in Ganjam, Gajapati, Rayagada, Koraput and Malkangiri districts tomorrow. Heavy rain may trigger waterlogging, flash floods and landslides, while strong winds could damage power lines and disrupt communication. The State Government has intensified preparedness, with rescue teams on standby and ministers assigned to monitor vulnerable districts. Educational institutions in six districts will remain closed tomorrow and the day after tomorrow. Fishermen have been advised not to venture into the sea. Meanwhile, Railways have cancelled several services and curtailed others, including the Hirakhand Express, which will terminate at Rayagada instead of Jagdalpur. Passengers have been advised to check the latest train status before travelling.

national_raw_news.title: 9th Asian Champions Trophy Hockey Tournament begins today 59 mins ago 16
national_raw_news.content: The 9th Hero Hockey Men’s Asian Champions Trophy 2026 is starting today in Punjab. The opening ceremony and league match of this week-long hockey extravaganza will be held at the Olympian Surjit Hockey Stadium in Jalandhar. Six leading hockey nations, including host India, Malaysia, China, Japan, South Korea, and Bangladesh, are participating in this first major continental hockey tournament being organized in Punjab. Akashvani’s all-InderDhanush channels, along with Jalandhar’s Primary Channel, will broadcast live commentary of matches played by India and the semi-finals and final as well. Entry to the venues is free. Olympian Surjit Hockey Stadium, Jalandhar and Olympian Balbir Singh Senior International Hockey Stadium, Mohali, both have been renovated as per world standards and are ready for the matches. Starting from tomorrow, there will be three matches each day, including matches under floodlights, till November 2nd in Jalandhar. The final and semi-finals will be played at the Mohali stadium on November 4th and 5th. The pool matches would start with the opening match between India and Bangladesh under floodlights. Two matches between Malaysia and China and Japan v/s South Korea will be played during the day. The teams have already reached Punjab and were given a warm traditional Punjabi welcome. The glittering ‘Hero Asian Champions Trophy – 2026’ has also reached Jalandhar after its week-long tour of various districts, which is the dream of every team competing in this prestigious championship.
